title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 1 — Environmental Studies | Civic Sense
description: Subject-wise test on Civic Sense (Environmental Studies) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 1. 25Q.
subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Where should we throw waste paper and fruit peels?

options.text: On the road
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because throwing waste on the road contributes to pollution and makes the environment dirty.

options.text: Under the bench
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because throwing waste under the bench is not a proper way to dispose of waste and can attract pests.

options.text: In the dustbin
options.explanation: This option is correct because throwing waste in the dustbin is the proper way to dispose of waste and keeps the surroundings clean.

options.text: Anywhere
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because throwing waste anywhere can contribute to pollution and make the environment dirty.

questions.explanation: Throwing waste in the dustbin keeps our surroundings clean and tidy, which is a good civic sense and prevents pollution.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: What should you say when your friend gives you a pencil to use?

options.text: Give it back
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because giving the pencil back immediately after receiving it is not a polite response.

options.text: Thank you
options.explanation: This option is correct because saying 'thank you' is a polite way to respond when someone gives you something.

options.text: Nothing
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because not responding at all is impolite and shows a lack of gratitude.

options.text: I want more
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because asking for more after receiving something is greedy and impolite.

questions.explanation: Saying 'Thank you' shows politeness and gratitude, which are important parts of good civic sense and good manners.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: When you walk on the road, where should you walk to be safe?

options.text: In the middle of the road
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because walking in the middle of the road is dangerous and can lead to accidents.

options.text: On the footpath
options.explanation: This option is correct because walking on the footpath is the safest way to walk on the road, away from traffic.

options.text: Very close to moving cars
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because walking close to moving cars is dangerous and can lead to accidents.

options.text: On the opposite side of the road
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because walking on the opposite side of the road may not always be safe, especially if there is no footpath.

questions.explanation: Walking on the footpath keeps you safe from traffic and is the correct way to use public roads, preventing accidents.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: What should you do when an elder person needs help carrying something heavy?

options.text: Run away
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because running away from someone who needs help is not only impolite but also unkind.

options.text: Ignore them
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because ignoring someone who needs help shows a lack of empathy and kindness.

options.text: Offer to help them
options.explanation: This option is correct because offering help to someone in need, especially an elder, demonstrates respect, kindness, and good civic sense.

options.text: Laugh at them
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because laughing at someone who needs help is not only unkind but also disrespectful.

questions.explanation: Helping elders shows respect and kindness, which are important aspects of good civic sense and community living.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: You are playing in the park and see someone plucking flowers from the garden. What should you do?

options.text: Pluck flowers too
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because plucking flowers contributes to the damage of the garden and is not a responsible action.

options.text: Tell them politely not to pluck flowers
options.explanation: This option is correct because politely telling someone not to pluck flowers is a respectful way to address the issue and help maintain the garden.

options.text: Ignore them and keep playing
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because ignoring the situation does not address the problem and allows the damage to continue.

options.text: Shout at them loudly
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because shouting is not a polite or effective way to address the issue and may escalate the situation.

questions.explanation: Plucking flowers damages plants in public spaces. Politely telling someone not to do it helps maintain the beauty of the park for everyone.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: When you are waiting for your turn at the school canteen or bus stop, what is the best way to wait?

options.text: Push others to go first
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because pushing others is not only impolite but also unfair and can lead to conflicts.

options.text: Stand anywhere you want
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because standing anywhere can lead to disorganization and unfairness in waiting for one's turn.

options.text: Wait in a queue (line)
options.explanation: This option is correct because waiting in a queue is an organized and fair way to wait for one's turn, showing respect for others.

options.text: Run around
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because running around while waiting is not only unsafe but also disruptive and disrespectful to others.

questions.explanation: Waiting in a queue shows patience and respect for others, ensuring everyone gets their turn in an organized and fair manner.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Why is it important to keep our school and classroom clean?

options.text: So that we can play more
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because while cleanliness can contribute to a better environment for play, it is not the primary reason for keeping the school and classroom clean.

options.text: Because it looks nice and keeps us healthy
options.explanation: This option is correct because a clean environment is aesthetically pleasing, conducive to learning, and helps prevent the spread of illnesses.

options.text: So that teachers will give us chocolates
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because the primary motivation for keeping the school and classroom clean should not be based on receiving rewards like chocolates.

options.text: It is not important
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because keeping the school and classroom clean is indeed important for health, learning, and overall well-being.

questions.explanation: A clean environment is pleasant to be in, helps us learn better, and prevents the spread of germs, keeping everyone healthy.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Which of these actions shows good civic sense in a public place like a hospital or library?

options.text: Talking loudly on the phone
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because talking loudly on the phone in a hospital or library is disruptive and shows a lack of consideration for others.

options.text: Making a lot of noise
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because making a lot of noise in these settings is not only disruptive but also disrespectful to those who need quiet.

options.text: Keeping quiet and respecting others' peace
options.explanation: This option is correct because keeping quiet in hospitals and libraries shows respect for others who are there for medical care or study, and helps maintain a peaceful environment.

options.text: Running around and playing games
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because running around and playing games in a hospital or library is inappropriate, disruptive, and can be dangerous.

questions.explanation: Hospitals and libraries are places where people need quiet to rest or concentrate. Keeping quiet shows consideration for others.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Rohan is walking in a crowded market and sees a small child who is crying and seems lost. What should Rohan do first?

options.text: Try to take the child home by himself
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because taking a lost child home alone can be unsafe for both the child and Rohan, and may not be the child's actual home.

options.text: Give the child some candy and leave
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because giving the child candy and leaving does not address the child's lost situation and can be seen as irresponsible.

options.text: Go to the nearest shopkeeper or a police officer and tell them about the child
options.explanation: This option is correct because informing a responsible adult, such as a shopkeeper or police officer, is the safest and most responsible action to help a lost child find their parents or guardians.

options.text: Ignore the child and continue walking
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because ignoring a lost child is not only unkind but also irresponsible, as the child may be in distress and need help.

questions.explanation: For a Class 1 child, the best and safest action when seeing a lost child is to inform a responsible adult (like a shopkeeper, security guard, or police officer) rather than trying to help alone.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Imagine if everyone threw their garbage on the streets instead of in dustbins. What would be the most likely result?

options.text: The streets would look very colorful
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because throwing garbage on the streets would not make them look colorful; instead, it would lead to a dirty and polluted environment.

options.text: The streets would become dirty, smell bad, and spread diseases
options.explanation: This option is correct because littering and not disposing of waste properly leads to dirty streets, unpleasant odors, and can spread diseases due to the accumulation of garbage and potential breeding of pests.

options.text: We would have more space to walk
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because throwing garbage on the streets would actually reduce the space available to walk, as the garbage would occupy the space and make it difficult to navigate.

options.text: Animals would find more food easily
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because while animals might find more food, this would not be a positive outcome as it would attract pests, create unhealthy conditions, and potentially harm the animals themselves.

questions.explanation: This question requires understanding the negative consequences of a widespread lack of civic sense. Littering causes unsanitary conditions, bad odors, and can lead to health problems and a polluted environment.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: What should you use to throw away rubbish like a candy wrapper after eating in the park?

options.text: The ground
options.explanation: Throwing rubbish on the ground makes the environment dirty.

options.text: Your pocket
options.explanation: Keeping rubbish in your pocket does not dispose of it properly.

options.text: A dustbin
options.explanation: A dustbin is the appropriate place for disposing of rubbish.

options.text: Under a tree
options.explanation: Throwing rubbish under a tree is not a proper way to dispose of it.

questions.explanation: Throwing rubbish in a dustbin keeps our surroundings clean and is a basic act of good civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: How should you talk to your teachers, parents, and other elders?

options.text: Loudly and demandingly
options.explanation: Speaking loudly and demandingly is not respectful.

options.text: Rudely and disrespectfully
options.explanation: Speaking rudely and disrespectfully is not acceptable.

options.text: Politely and respectfully
options.explanation: Polite and respectful speech is a sign of good manners.

options.text: By shouting to get attention
options.explanation: Shouting to get attention is not a respectful way to communicate.

questions.explanation: Speaking politely and respectfully shows good manners and is an important part of civic sense, especially towards elders.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Where is the safest place to cross a busy road?

options.text: Anywhere you want, quickly
options.explanation: Crossing anywhere is not safe and can be dangerous.

options.text: From between two parked cars
options.explanation: Crossing from between parked cars can be hazardous.

options.text: At the zebra crossing
options.explanation: Zebra crossings are designated safe areas for pedestrians to cross.

options.text: While running across the road
options.explanation: Running across the road is not safe and can lead to accidents.

questions.explanation: Crossing at a zebra crossing is a traffic rule designed for pedestrian safety and demonstrates good civic sense by following rules.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: You see a water tap running in your school playground, even though no one is using it. What is the best thing you should do?

options.text: Ignore it and keep playing.
options.explanation: Ignoring a running tap wastes water.

options.text: Tell your friends to play with the water.
options.explanation: Playing with the water does not address the issue of the running tap.

options.text: Close the tap tightly.
options.explanation: Closing the tap conserves water and is a responsible action.

options.text: Wait for someone else to close it.
options.explanation: Waiting for someone else to close the tap does not take initiative.

questions.explanation: Closing a running tap saves water, which is a precious resource, and shows responsibility and good civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: If you are waiting for your turn to get on the school bus or buy something, what is the proper way to behave?

options.text: Push others to get in first.
options.explanation: Pushing others is not fair and can cause conflict.

options.text: Stand in a line (queue) patiently.
options.explanation: Standing in a line shows respect for others and follows a fair process.

options.text: Run to the front of the line.
options.explanation: Running to the front of the line is not fair to others.

options.text: Block the way for others.
options.explanation: Blocking the way for others is not considerate and can cause problems.

questions.explanation: Standing in a queue ensures fairness, order, and prevents chaos, which are important aspects of good civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Why is it important not to write or draw on public walls, like school walls or park walls?

options.text: Because it makes the walls look pretty.
options.explanation: Writing or drawing on walls does not necessarily make them look pretty.

options.text: Because it is fun to do.
options.explanation: While it might be fun, it is not a good reason to deface public property.

options.text: Because it spoils public property and makes places look dirty.
options.explanation: Defacing public property can make it look dirty and neglected.

options.text: Because no one will see it.
options.explanation: People can see the damage, and it reflects poorly on the community.

questions.explanation: Public property belongs to everyone, and defacing it shows a lack of civic responsibility. Keeping public places clean and cared for is good civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: You are playing with your new toy car and your friend wants to play with it too. What does it show if you let your friend play with your toy?

options.text: That you don't like your toy car.
options.explanation: Letting a friend play with your toy does not necessarily mean you don't like it.

options.text: That you are a good and kind friend.
options.explanation: Sharing with a friend shows kindness and a willingness to be generous.

options.text: That you want your friend to give you new toys.
options.explanation: Letting a friend play with your toy does not imply that you want new toys in return.

options.text: That you have too many toys.
options.explanation: Letting a friend play with your toy does not indicate that you have too many toys.

questions.explanation: Sharing is a kind and considerate act that promotes friendship and good social behavior, which is an important part of civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Statement 1: We should always keep our classroom clean. Statement 2: A clean classroom helps us learn better and stay healthy. Which option correctly describes the relationship between these two statements?

options.text: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 explains the reasoning behind Statement 1.

options.text: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 explains the reasoning behind Statement 1.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true, and Statement 2 explains Statement 1.
options.explanation: Statement 2 provides the reason why Statement 1 is important.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1.
options.explanation: Statement 2 does explain the importance of Statement 1.

questions.explanation: Keeping the classroom clean (Statement 1) is a good civic habit. The reason for this is that a clean environment contributes to better learning and health (Statement 2), thus Statement 2 explains Statement 1.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Rohan is walking to school. He sees an old lady struggling to carry her heavy grocery bags and trying to cross the busy road. What is the most helpful thing Rohan can do?

options.text: Walk past quickly and pretend not to see her.
options.explanation: Ignoring someone in need is not a kind or helpful action.

options.text: Tell her to wait for someone else to help.
options.explanation: Telling her to wait for someone else does not provide immediate assistance.

options.text: Offer to help her carry the bags and cross the road safely.
options.explanation: Offering to help is a kind and responsible action that shows empathy.

options.text: Point at her and laugh.
options.explanation: Pointing and laughing is not only unhelpful but also disrespectful.

questions.explanation: Offering help to someone in need, especially an elder, is a core aspect of kindness, empathy, and good civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Which of these actions is NOT considered a good civic habit?

options.text: Throwing waste in a dustbin.
options.explanation: Throwing waste in a dustbin is a good civic habit.

options.text: Helping an old person.
options.explanation: Helping an old person is a kind and responsible action.

options.text: Keeping public places clean.
options.explanation: Keeping public places clean is important for the community.

options.text: Littering on the road.
options.explanation: Littering harms the environment and is not a good civic habit.

questions.explanation: Littering on the road makes the environment dirty, harms nature, and is disrespectful to public spaces, therefore it is not a good civic habit.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: What is the best thing to do with a chocolate wrapper after eating the chocolate in a public park?

options.text: Throw it on the ground near a tree.
options.explanation: Throwing waste on the ground contributes to pollution and makes public places dirty.

options.text: Keep it in your hand until you find a dustbin.
options.explanation: This action helps maintain cleanliness in public areas.

options.text: Give it to your friend to hold.
options.explanation: Giving waste to someone else does not solve the problem of disposing of it properly.

options.text: Hide it under a bench.
options.explanation: Hiding waste does not dispose of it properly and can still contribute to pollution.

questions.explanation: Keeping waste with you until you find a dustbin helps keep public places clean and tidy, which is a good civic habit.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: When you are waiting in a queue to get on a school bus, what should you do?

options.text: Push the person in front of you to move faster.
options.explanation: Pushing someone is disrespectful and can be harmful.

options.text: Stand quietly and wait for your turn.
options.explanation: This behavior demonstrates respect for others and patience.

options.text: Run to the front of the line.
options.explanation: Cutting in line is unfair to others who are waiting.

options.text: Talk loudly and disturb others.
options.explanation: Being loud can disturb others and is not considerate.

questions.explanation: Standing quietly and waiting for your turn in a queue shows patience and respect for others, which is an important part of civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: You see a small child crying because they have lost their toy in the playground. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore them and continue playing.
options.explanation: Ignoring someone in need can be hurtful and shows a lack of empathy.

options.text: Laugh at them for losing their toy.
options.explanation: Laughing at someone's misfortune is not kind and can make them feel worse.

options.text: Ask them what happened and try to help them find the toy or inform an elder.
options.explanation: This action demonstrates kindness and a willingness to help.

options.text: Take their toy if you find it.
options.explanation: Taking something that doesn't belong to you is not right, even if you found it.

questions.explanation: Helping someone in distress, especially a younger child, shows kindness and responsibility towards others, which is a key aspect of civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Imagine you are in the school library, and you finish reading a book. What is the correct way to put it back?

options.text: Leave it on any table you find.
options.explanation: Leaving a book on any table can make the library disorganized.

options.text: Put it back on the shelf from where you took it, in the correct place.
options.explanation: This action helps maintain the library's organization and makes books easy to find.

options.text: Throw it into a pile of books.
options.explanation: Throwing a book into a pile can damage it and contribute to disorganization.

options.text: Give it to your friend to put away.
options.explanation: Giving the responsibility to someone else does not ensure the book will be put back correctly.

questions.explanation: Returning things to their proper place, especially in shared spaces like a library, helps keep the place organized and makes it easy for others to find what they need. This is a good example of respecting public property and showing civic sense.
questions.subject: maha1-evs

questions.question: Rina is playing in the school garden. She thinks of plucking flowers to make a garland. Why should she not do this?

options.text: Because the flowers might have thorns.
options.explanation: The presence of thorns is not the main reason for not plucking flowers in a public garden.

options.text: Because plucking flowers spoils the beauty of the garden for everyone else.
options.explanation: This is the correct reason as it considers the impact on others and the preservation of public property.

options.text: Because Rina should only play with toys.
options.explanation: This option does not address the issue of plucking flowers in a public garden.

options.text: Because the flowers might make her sneeze.
options.explanation: Allergic reactions are not the main concern in this context.

questions.explanation: Public gardens are for everyone to enjoy. Plucking flowers damages the plants and spoils the beauty of the shared space, showing a lack of respect for public property and other people's enjoyment. Good civic sense means preserving shared resources.
questions.subject: maha1-evs
